sources.entry: NGINX - HTTP and reverse proxy server, mail proxy server, and generic TCP/UDP proxy server. (Source Code) BSD-2-Clause C/deb/Docker

summary.one_liner: NGINX is an open-source web server that also serves as a reverse proxy, load balancer, API gateway, mail proxy and content cache.
summary.what_it_does: NGINX is a high-performance HTTP server and reverse proxy that can also act as a load balancer, API gateway and content cache, per the README. It runs as a master process that manages worker processes, which scale with CPU cores and share state through shared memory zones. Functionality is split into modules that are either compiled statically into the binary or built and loaded dynamically; the README names NGINX JavaScript (njs) as a popular dynamic module. Configuration is done through text files with directives, and `nginx -V` shows which static modules a binary includes. The README covers installing prebuilt packages from the official repository (stable and mainline branches), building from source with auto/configure and make, and getting started with TLS, load balancing, rate limiting and caching via linked guides.
use_cases: serve static websites and web applications
reverse proxy in front of backend servers
notable: Modular design with static and dynamic modules
Multi-process architecture with worker processes sharing memory zones
Official binaries for Linux, FreeBSD and an experimental Windows build
caveats: The Windows build is a proof-of-concept intended only for development and testing, per the README
Enterprise distributions and commercial support are offered by F5, Inc.
The README gives only a minimal build dependency list; additional modules need extra libraries
